messages:
ria: Heads up — ran into a weird Android-only SDK issue today. App was uploading large logs and we started seeing hung requests + duplicate parts when a 302 redirect + 401 refresh happened mid-upload. Repro in instrumented sample.
dave: hmm 302 + 401 during upload? How is redirect handled by OkHttp in our client?
miguel: by default OkHttp will follow redirects automatically. If followRedirects is true it may create a new request (with a different URL) and that interacts badly with our Authenticator refresh flow.
dave: so sequence is: POST -> server responds 302 to a different host (or path) -> client follows -> new host returns 401 -> authenticator refresh runs -> request replay tries to re-send streaming body and sometimes fails/duplicates?
ia: yup. On Android the InputStream-based RequestBody can't be re-read; sometimes call blocks until timeout, other times the app sees partial duplicate data on server. Also saw some ANR reports when writeTimeout wasn't set and the write blocked indefinitely.
miguel: can you paste the client config?
ria: sure:
```java
OkHttpClient client = new OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(true)
  .followRedirects(true)
  .followSslRedirects(true)
  .connectTimeout(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .writeTimeout(0, TimeUnit.SECONDS) // oops
  .authenticator(myAuthenticator)
  .build();
```
ria: writeTimeout was 0 in our sample (we shipped a default that means no timeout). That explains ANRs when write blocks.
dave: set a sane writeTimeout and readTimeout for mobile. Also consider disabling automatic followRedirects for upload endpoints so the app can handle redirects explicitly and rebuild bodies.
miguel: another pattern: move token refresh out of Authenticator to a network Interceptor that refreshes ahead-of-time when 401 seen and then throws a clear exception so caller can retry with a repeatable body if needed. Authenticator is nice because OkHttp will retry transparently, but that assumes bodies are repeatable.
dave: agree. For the SDK samples we should: 1) show recommended OkHttp config for uploads (retryOnConnectionFailure=false, followRedirects=false, finite timeouts), 2) provide a File-backed RequestBody helper and a streaming-safe retry pattern, 3) include an instrumented test that simulates 302->401 redirect flow.
miguel: helper we use in sample (stream -> temp file):
```java
static RequestBody tempFileRequestBody(InputStream in, MediaType mt, Context ctx) throws IOException {
  File f = File.createTempFile("up", "bin", ctx.getCacheDir());
  try (OutputStream os = new FileOutputStream(f)) {
    byte[] b = new byte[8192];
    int r;
    while ((r = in.read(b)) != -1) os.write(b,0,r);
  }
  return RequestBody.create(mt, f);
}
```
miguel: downside is disk + latency. Alternative: use resumable/chunked uploads via our API (preferable). If customers upload large media on mobile, recommend chunked/resumable endpoints.
ria: also added runtime warning in our sample wrapper: if client.authenticator != null and request.body() != null and request.body() instanceof OneShotBody -> log.warn("Authenticator + non-repeatable body may cause duplicate uploads")
dave: good. I'd also add a linter rule in the SDK repo to flag usage of InputStreamRequestBody in combination with setting an authenticator on the client during build. At minimum we should document it on the Android SDK onboarding page.
miguel: CI bot created issue #3899: "Android SDK: sample + docs for uploads — redirects, auth refresh, and timeouts" https://github.com/redwood-inference/android-samples/issues/3899 :robot_face:
build-bot: Created PR draft #412 in android-samples with test harness and temp-file helper (needs review).
ria: I'll update the onboarding quickstart to call out: "For mobile uploads: set finite writeTimeout, prefer resumable uploads, avoid followRedirects=true for upload endpoints, and prefer file-backed bodies when using authenticators." Tagging @dave @miguel for review. Thanks :thumbsup:
